title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 29-31). A 'figure' F is a family of closed subsets of a space such that every point x of the support |F| = ∪F lies in a smallest member of F. That member's 'open stratum' A°(F) is A minus the members of F strictly contained in A.

The notes use three relations:
- F' ≪ F: F' is subordinate to, or refines, F.
- F' ≼ F: subdivision, i.e. refinement with |F'| = |F|.
- G ≤ F: G is a closed subfigure of F, equivalently G = {A ∈ F | A ⊂ |G|}.

Grothendieck is checking the axioms of an axiomatic 'algebra of figures'. Axiom C6 concerns the product F.G (made of the A∩B with A°∩B° ≠ ∅). On this page he verifies Axiom C7: if G ≤ F and G' ≼ G is a subdivision of the closed subfigure, then G' extends to a subdivision F' of F inducing G' on G. The candidate (end of p. 29) is F' = G' ∪ (F\G).

a) F' is a figure.
- Support: |F'| = |G'| ∪ |F\G|, with |G'| = |G| and |F\G| ⊃ |F|\|G|. Hence |F'| ⊃ |F|, and trivially |F'| ⊂ |F|, so |F'| = |F|.
- Smallest member, case 1, x ∈ |G| = |G'|. Take A ∈ G' with x ∈ A°(G'), and let B ∈ F' contain x. If B ∈ G', then A ⊂ B by minimality in G'. If B ∈ F\G, then A°(G') ∩ B ≠ ∅, so A° ⊂ B, hence A ⊂ B.
- Smallest member, case 2, x ∉ |G|. Every member of F' containing x lies in F\G. The smallest member A of F containing x is not in G, so it lies in F\G ⊂ F'. It is a fortiori smallest there.

b) F' subdivides F. Since the supports agree, it remains to show F' refines F.
- (1) For A ∈ F', the set F^A = {B ∈ F | A ⊂ B} has a least element. Take A itself if A ∈ F\G; if A ∈ G', this follows from G' ≪ F.
- (2) For A ∈ F' and B ∈ F, A∩B is a union of strata of F'. If A ∈ G', it is a union of strata of G' (since G' ≪ F), and these are also strata of F'. The case A ∈ F\G is finished on p. 31.

Page 31 goes on to characterise this F' as the canonical extension: the map F'→F restricts to a bijection F'\G' ≅ F\G, equivalently F' ⊃ F\G.

In modern terms: extending a refinement of a closed sub-stratification to a refinement of the whole stratification, by keeping the strata off the subspace unchanged. It is the analogue of 'a subdivision of a subcomplex extends to a subdivision of the complex' in PL topology. Here it is trivial because strata are not required to be cells.
errors: Case 1 step 'A°(G') ∩ B ≠ ∅ ⇒ A° ⊂ B' is asserted without proof. It needs two facts: B∩|G| is a union of strata of G (from G ≤ F and the stratification property of F), and strata of G are unions of strata of G' (since G' ≼ G).
Passing from A° ⊂ B to A ⊂ B tacitly uses that A is the closure of A° (or that every point of A lies in A° or in a smaller member also contained in B), together with B closed.
In b)2° the claim that strata of G' are strata of F' uses implicitly that no member of F\G is contained in |G|. This is true because G is closed (an initial segment) in F, but it is not stated.
Minor: for each x, the existence of the smallest-member set A ∈ G' with x ∈ A°(G') is quoted without comment (it is the figure property of G').

ideas.what: Axiom C7: a subdivision G' of a closed subfigure G ≤ F extends to a subdivision F' = G' ∪ (F\G) of F inducing G' on G
ideas.modern_name: Extension of refinements from a closed sub-stratification (cf. extending subdivisions of subcomplexes in PL topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: PL topology folklore (Zeeman, Hudson, Rourke–Sanderson for complexes); no specific credit for abstract stratifications
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA; the tame topology programme of Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5) is related in spirit but has no such axiom

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'algebra of figures': finite closed families with smallest-member property, strata A°, relations ≪, ≼, ≤, product F.G, axioms C1–C7
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial/poset-theoretic axiomatics of stratifications (closest: poset-stratified spaces, Lurie HA App. A; cell-like stratifications)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Various (Whitney/Thom/Mather for stratifications; Lurie and others for poset-stratified spaces)
ideas.where_published: Motivation in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (tame topology, dévissage of stratified structures); the figure formalism itself appears unpublished

missed.claim: The page is a routine verification step in an unpublished axiomatic framework ('algèbre des figures', axioms C1–C7) for stratified, tame-topology-style structures. The framework as a whole seems undocumented in the literature, but this page adds nothing beyond the trivial extension lemma.
missed.quote: On prend F' = G' ∪ (F\G) ... Il faut vérifier a) c'est une figure b) que [F'] subdivise F c) qui induit G' sur G.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents part of Grothendieck's 1986 attempt to axiomatise tame topology combinatorially. That may interest work on o-minimal and poset-stratified foundations, but the content here is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, essentially trivial verification (extension of a subdivision from a closed subfigure by keeping the complementary pieces) inside an unpublished axiomatic framework. It is correct up to small implicit steps and contains nothing a specialist would find new beyond the existence of the framework itself.
transcription_corrections: 'soit A ∈ G'^°' should read 'soit A ∈ G'' (the superscript is a stray mark); the condition is x ∈ A°(G').
Case 1 reads: 'Si B ∈ G', c'est évident. Si B ∈ F\G, alors A°(G') ∩ B ≠ ∅, donc A° ⊂ B OK'. The struck words are '[B contient]'.

'b) F' [-affine-] {+raffine+} F' is more plausibly 'b) F' subdivise F' with a correction, consistent with p. 29 'b) que [F'] subdivise F'. The next line indeed says 'il faut voir seulement que F' raffine F'.
In b)2°, the insertion reads roughly 'A∩B est réunion dans F'' (i.e. a union of strata of F'), as made explicit in the following line.
The last line ends 'qui sont aussi des strates de F''.
